chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who said: Some of our companions narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Humayd, from Ya'qub al-Qummi, from his brother Imran ibn Abdillah al-Qummi, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him).
Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'Fight those polytheists who are near you,' he said: 'The Daylamites.'

key_terms.الدَّيْلَمُ: The Daylamites, a specific ethnic group from the Daylam region in northern Iran, identified here as the referent of the Quranic verse.
key_terms.الْكُفَّارِ: Polytheists or disbelievers, referring to those who do not accept Islam.
key_terms.يَلُونَكُمْ: Those who are near you or adjacent to you, indicating geographical proximity.

ai.seo_question: Who are the Daylamites in the context of Quranic exegesis?
ai.summary: In this rare narration (nadir) from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) offers a specific exegetical identification of the 'polytheists near you' in Surah At-Tawbah as the Daylamites, a distinct ethnic group from northern Iran. This highlights the Shia scholarly tradition of linking general Quranic injunctions to specific historical contexts and communities, demonstrating how divine commands were applied to contemporary adversaries of the early Muslim community.
